title: Strained Yoghurt Labneh with Olive Oil and Fresh Mint
summary: Full-fat yoghurt is salted and strained through muslin in the fridge for a day until thick and spreadable, then swirled into a bowl and finished with olive oil, dried mint and fresh mint leaves.
equipment: 2 layers of muslin or a clean thin tea towel

ingredients.item: full-fat plain Greek-style yoghurt (no gelling agents or thickeners)
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Stir the salt into the yoghurt until dissolved.

steps.title: Line the sieve
steps.text: Set a sieve over a deep bowl and line it with damp muslin.

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Spoon in the yoghurt, cover and strain in the fridge for 24 hours.

steps.title: Check the texture
steps.text: It should be as thick as soft cream cheese; strain longer for firmer labneh.

steps.title: Plate
steps.text: Spoon into a shallow bowl and make a swirl with a well in the middle.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Fill the well with olive oil, add both mints and serve chilled.

tips: Use yoghurt without gelling agents or thickeners, or it will not drain properly.
Leave plenty of space under the sieve so the cloth never sits in the whey.
Roll very firm labneh into balls and keep them under olive oil in the fridge.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 1 week. Firm labneh balls kept under olive oil last up to 2 weeks in the fridge. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
